mechanism: Additive anticoagulant/antiplatelet effects
effect: Significantly increased risk of major bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage
recommendation: Avoid combination unless specifically indicated. Monitor INR closely if unavoidable.

mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and may increase Warfarin levels via CYP2C9 inhibition
effect: Increased risk of GI bleeding and elevated INR
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in patients on Warfarin. Use Paracetamol for pain relief.

mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and may increase Warfarin levels
effect: Increased risk of GI bleeding and elevated INR
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use Paracetamol as alternative analgesic.

mechanism: NSAID antiplatelet effect plus potential CYP2C9 inhibition
recommendation: Avoid combination.

mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9, reducing Warfarin metabolism
recommendation: If combination necessary, reduce Warfarin dose and monitor INR every 2-3 days.

mechanism: Strong CYP2C9 inhibition by Fluconazole
effect: Markedly increased INR and bleeding risk
recommendation: Reduce Warfarin dose by 25-50% and monitor INR closely.

mechanism: Fluoroquinolones may inhibit Warfarin metabolism and alter gut flora
recommendation: Monitor INR closely. Consider alternative antibiotic.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase Warfarin levels
recommendation: Monitor INR. Use Azithromycin as safer alternative.

mechanism: Omeprazole may slightly inhibit CYP2C19 affecting R-warfarin
recommendation: Monitor INR when starting/stopping. Generally well-tolerated.

mechanism: Contrast media may cause acute kidney injury, increasing Metformin accumulation
recommendation: Hold Metformin 48 hours before and after contrast administration.

mechanism: Both increase serum potassium
effect: Risk of hyperkalemia, potentially life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias
recommendation: Monitor potassium closely. Avoid in renal impairment.

mechanism: Dual RAAS blockade
effect: Increased risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and renal impairment
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use one agent only.

mechanism: Amoxicillin may reduce Phenytoin absorption
effect: Decreased Phenytoin levels, risk of breakthrough seizures
recommendation: Monitor Phenytoin levels. Separate administration by 2 hours if possible.

mechanism: Both are CYP enzyme inducers, complex mutual interactions
effect: Unpredictable changes in levels of both drugs
recommendation: Monitor levels of both drugs closely.

mechanism: Complex interaction: Phenytoin initially increases then decreases Warfarin effect
recommendation: Monitor INR very frequently. Consider alternative anticonvulsant.

mechanism: Valproic acid displaces Phenytoin from protein binding and inhibits metabolism
effect: Initially increased free Phenytoin levels (toxicity risk), then decreased total levels
recommendation: Monitor free Phenytoin levels, not total levels.

mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP1A2, reducing Theophylline clearance
effect: Increased Theophylline levels — risk of toxicity (seizures, arrhythmias)
recommendation: Avoid combination or reduce Theophylline dose by 25%. Monitor levels.

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, reducing Theophylline clearance
recommendation: Reduce Theophylline dose by 30-50%. Use Levofloxacin as alternative.

mechanism: CYP3A4/CYP1A2 inhibition
recommendation: Monitor Theophylline levels. Consider Azithromycin (minimal interaction).

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein, reducing Digoxin renal clearance
recommendation: Reduce Digoxin dose by 50% when starting Amiodarone.

mechanism: Furosemide causes hypokalemia, increasing Digoxin sensitivity
effect: Increased risk of Digoxin toxicity and cardiac arrhythmias
recommendation: Monitor potassium levels. Supplement potassium as needed.

mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition increases Simvastatin levels dramatically
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED. Use Azithromycin or switch statin to Rosuvastatin.

mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED. Suspend statin during clarithromycin course.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases Atorvastatin exposure
recommendation: Limit Atorvastatin to 20mg during Clarithromycin course. Monitor for muscle pain.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition
recommendation: Consider temporary statin suspension or switch to Rosuvastatin.

mechanism: Beta-blockers antagonize beta-2 bronchodilation
recommendation: Use cardioselective beta-blocker at lowest dose. Monitor respiratory status.

mechanism: Additive bradycardic effect
effect: Risk of severe bradycardia and AV block
recommendation: Monitor heart rate and ECG. Start with low doses.

mechanism: Additive negative chronotropic and hypotensive effects
recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate. Often used together with caution.

mechanism: Both increase serotonin; Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 reducing Tramadol metabolism
effect: Risk of serotonin syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, myoclonus) and seizures
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use alternative analgesic.

mechanism: Additive serotonergic effect
recommendation: Avoid combination if possible. If used, start low and monitor closely.

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of Clopidogrel to active metabolite
effect: Reduced antiplatelet effect, increased cardiovascular event risk
recommendation: Use Pantoprazole instead (less CYP2C19 inhibition).

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of Methotrexate
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with high-dose Methotrexate. Monitor levels.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs. If necessary, monitor lithium levels closely.

mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, retaining potassium
recommendation: Monitor potassium levels. Avoid routine potassium supplementation.

mechanism: Antacids chelate Ciprofloxacin, reducing absorption
recommendation: Take Ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids.

mechanism: Metal ions chelate tetracyclines
recommendation: Separate administration by 2-3 hours.

mechanism: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, increasing Simvastatin levels
recommendation: Limit Simvastatin to 20mg when combined with Amlodipine.

mechanism: Erythromycin strongly inhibits CYP3A4, markedly increasing Carbamazepine levels
recommendation: AVOID combination. Use Azithromycin as alternative.

mechanism: Complex bidirectional interaction affecting metabolism of both drugs
effect: Decreased Valproic Acid levels, increased active Carbamazepine metabolite
recommendation: Monitor levels of both drugs. Adjust doses accordingly.

mechanism: Amoxicillin may alter gut flora affecting vitamin K synthesis
recommendation: Monitor INR during antibiotic course.

mechanism: Antacids reduce Gabapentin bioavailability by ~20%
recommendation: Take Gabapentin at least 2 hours after antacids.

mechanism: Both are ototoxic and nephrotoxic
effect: Increased risk of hearing loss and kidney damage
recommendation: Avoid combination if possible. Monitor renal function and hearing.

mechanism: Non-selective beta-blockade antagonizes beta-2 bronchodilation
effect: Severe bronchospasm, loss of asthma control
recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED in asthma. Use cardioselective beta-blocker (Metoprolol) if needed.

mechanism: Beta-blockers mask hypoglycemia symptoms (tachycardia, tremor)
recommendation: Educate patient on non-adrenergic hypoglycemia symptoms (sweating, hunger).

mechanism: Alcohol inhibits gluconeogenesis and increases lactate production
effect: Increased risk of lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia
recommendation: Limit alcohol consumption. Avoid binge drinking.

mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2C9, increasing Phenytoin levels
recommendation: Monitor Phenytoin levels. Consider alternative antidepressant.

mechanism: Both increase serum potassium
recommendation: Monitor potassium closely, especially in renal impairment.

mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effect
recommendation: Often intentionally combined (dual antiplatelet therapy). Monitor for bleeding signs.
